(By Sri.M.A.Patil, Advocate)
 JUDGMENT Sons of Venkatamma filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and Insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 alleging that on 19.01.2024 at 6.30 p.m., when Venkatamma was standing beside Sidlaghatta-Kolar main road at Thaladummanahalli gate bus stop, the rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40- EH-8497 rode the same negligently dashed the same to Venkatamma, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Venkatamma.

Immediately after accident,
Venkatamma had been shifted to Govt. Hospital, Siddlaghatta, wherein first aid has been provided,
then admitted to Govt. hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein on 20.01.2024 Venkatamma succumbed to the injuries.
2. Regarding accident Siddlaghatta Rural police registered a case in crime No.19/2024 against the rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497.

3. As on the date of accident, deceased Venkatamma being aged 60 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/-
p.m. by working as Coolie.
4. Inspite of service of notice to respondent No.1- owner of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2- Insurance company appeared through his advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident, age,
occupation and income of the deceased Venkatamma.
Respondent No.2-Insurance company asserted that the petitioners being aged children of Venkatamma, never depended on the income of Venkatamma.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 03.12.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 19.01.2024 at about 06.30 p.m., beside Siddlaghatta - Kolar Main road at Thaladummanahalli gate bus stop, in view of the negligent use of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EH-  8497, Motorcycle dashed to  Smt.Venkatamma, W/o.Anjinappa,
thereby caused accident resulting in the death of Venkatamma, W/o.Anjinappa?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, how much and from whom?

7. On 23.10.2024, 13.01.2025 petitioner No.2- Manjunath deposed as P.W.1 and produced 24 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.24.
On 13.1.2025 learned advocate appearing for respondent No.2 produced copy of the policy at Ex.R.1.
8. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Petitioners (all the children of Venkatamma) are entitle to receive Rs.10,17,028/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issues No.1:- In the evidence P.W.1 stated that on 19.01.2024 at 6.30 p.m., when his mother - Venkatamma was waiting beside Sidlaghatta-Kolar main road at Thaladummanahalli gate bus stop,
the rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 rode the same negligently from Sidlaghatta side towards Kolar, dashed the same to the Venkatamma, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Venkatamma.

Immediately after accident, Venkatamma had been shifted to Govt.
Hospital, Siddlaghatta, wherein first aid has been provided, then admitted to Govt. hospital,
Chikkaballapura, wherein on 20.01.2024 Venkatamma succumbed to the injuries.
11.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident.
12. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 submitted that he never witnessed the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.19/2024 registered by Siddlaghatta Rural police on 20.01.2024 at 9.00 hours against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC regarding the accident taken place on 19.01.2024 at 18.30 hours, resulting the death of Venkatamma, on the basis of the complaint presented by petitioner No.1- Nagaraj, S/o.Anjinappa.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of Sketch of place of accident, in which it is noted as the motorcycle which was running from western side to eastern side came to southern side (wrong side), caused accident.
Ex.P.5 is the vehicle seizure mahazar dated 20.01.2024.
Ex.P.6 is the Motor vehicles Accident Rreport dated 16.2.2024.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of Inquest Mahazar with enclosures.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of P.M. Report.
14.

Ex.P.9 is the copy of charge sheet filed by Siddlaghatta Rural police in crime No.19/2024 against the accused No.1-Madhu V., S/o.Venkatesh, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 for Nagaraja K A vs Madhu V on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117209848/
3 having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304-A of IPC.

sentences.text:
Ex.P.10 to 14 are the copy of statements of petitioner No.1, S/o.Anjinbappa, Prabhakara, S/o.Krishnappa, Govindappa,
S/o.Rangappa, Chandra T.K., S/o.Kempanna, Chandrashekar, S/o.Suryaprakash, Ex.P.18 to 20 are the OPD slip of Govt. Hosptial, Sidlaghatta, Govt. Hospital, Chikkaballapura.
15. In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence of P.W.1 regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

16. Hence, I have concluded that on 19.01.2024 at 6.30 p.m., when Venkatamma was standing beside Sidlaghatta-Kolar main road at Thaladummanahalli gate bus stop, the respondent No.1-Madhu negligently rode the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497, dashed the same to Venkatamma, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Venkatamma, who succumbed to those injuries on 20.01.2024.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

In the affidavit evidence P.W.1- Manjunatha stated that as on the date of accident his mother Venkatamma used to earn Rs.25,000/- per month by working as coolie and used to contribute entire income to the family.
18. In the written statement respondent No.2 Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of Venkatamma.

19. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of alleged incident himself and his brother never depended on the income of Venkatamma and as on the date of alleged incidcent his mother never earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of incident his mother was aged more than 62 years.
20. In the police records, age of Venkatamma is noted as 62 years as on the date of accident.
In the copy of ration card of the year 2013, age of Venkatamma is noted as 53 years.
In the copy of the Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.22 date of birth of Venkatamma is noted as 21.11.1960.
In the Ration card marked at Ex.P.21 Manjunath, Nagaraju, Munirathnamma and Anushka are noted as children of Venkatamma.
21. In the file there are no documents regarding quantum of income of deceased Venkatamma.

Hence, I have calculated the loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of deceased Venkatamma as on the 64 years date of accident - Notional income of the deceased as on the Rs.16,000/- date of accident - Less : 1/3rd deduction towards personal Rs.10,667/- expenses of the deceased (16,000 - 5,333= 10,667) Annual income of the deceased (10,667 x Rs.1,28,004/-
12) Loss of dependency 1,28,004 x 7 Rs.8,96,028/-

sentences.text:
Hence, I award compensation of Rs.8,96,028/- under the head Loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/-
towards loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.88,000/- towards consortium to petitioner No.1 & 2 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each.
Sl
. No .
Head of Compensation Amount/
Rs 1. Loss of dependency 8,96,028-00 2. Loss of estate 16,500-00 3. Funeral expenses 16,500-00 4. Loss of Consortium to 88,000-00 petitioners (44,000/- x 2) Total 10,17,028-00 23.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners (all the children) of deceased Venkatamma are entitle to receive Rs.10,17,028/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly.
24. Issue No.3: Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.1 shows as on the date of accident Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.

In reply, to the notice under Section 133 of IMV Act, marked at Ex.P.16 dated 17.2.2024 submitted by the respondent No.1 to the I.O. respondent No.1 noted the identification number of his Driving Licence.
Hence, it is clear that, respondent No.1 has not violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents No.1 and 2 to pay compensation to the petitioners (all children of Venkatamma), Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.10,17,028/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners (all the children of Venkatamma) towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EH-8497 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners (all children of Venkatamma) equally.

After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners (all the children of Venkatamma) may be released by Nagaraja K A vs Madhu V on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117209848/
5 crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer-I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 6th day of February, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
